# the contributor audits: exposed-face isolation, optimized atomic loss, and actual edge-credit curves



## Exposed-face isolation and optimized atomic certificates: PASS

Read `candidate 25fed51eab0d77f0` in full. A finite exposing base tilt keeps every trace on the chosen face exactly and excludes all other compact fibers. The nonzero-normal exception can be avoided. This works for the restriction of any finite Borel measure, including intrinsic Hausdorff measure with boundary mass; no dimension-dependent replacement measure is introduced. Taking infima and then the finite maximum over maximal anchored faces is legitimate. The unrestricted lower mass bound on those full face depths is consequently theorem-strength, not a completed reduction.

The six fibers over2Delta_2 are exact by exposed-edge convexity, and the body has positive ambient volume. The optimized atomic-certificate upper bound handles every representative choice. A noncollinear middle graph point is exposed within its three-point edge graph; a collinear one has height equal to the mean endpoint height and exact atomic depth equal to its own weight plus the smaller endpoint weight. The resulting bound1/2 is attained by the specified centroid selection. Thus this obstruction optimizes all one-point-per-fiber certificates using actual own-depth weights, not just the original centroids. It does not exclude actual continuous tail mass.

The two signed continuous-tail infima for the actual interval family are complete, including saturated endpoint cuts; pure integer caps have strictly larger mass. Maximization gives the exact actual raw depth7/8 and normalized7/36, so the example satisfies OC despite the weaker atomic certificate. Endpoint and off-face cap isolation retain all closed traces exactly.

## Three actual equal-endpoint source curves: PASS

Read `candidate 7a51de7a765ebba9` in full. Its additive midpoint source is the archived certificate in `candidate 9dc053aa681e5ef6`, whose own-fiber and endpoint contributions use distinct integer fibers. In particular the ordinary equal-endpoint three-fiber OC case was already covered; the new edge target is explicitly stronger.

The complementary Brunn--Minkowski estimate applies at g_K exactly as at g_M: the Minkowski midpoint of endpoint residuals lies in the opposite K cap, which ordinary Grunbaum bounds. The root-sum minimum at fixed residual total has the stated direction. The case endpoint captured mass>=v and all pure-integer normals are separately included. Each point belongs to the actual middle body.

The directional width formula decreases with its ratio above one and is symmetric under reciprocal ratios, so the stated eliminated bound follows from the audited width constraint. The candidate maximum and compact one-variable minimum are valid guaranteed curves, with no inference that a geometric extremizer realizes them. The range endpoints5/3,193/115 and3 follow from the displayed exact comparisons and the previously audited308/345 planar budget.

For translated equal-volume endpoints, their common ordinary centroid and the archived equal-body paired-centroid theorem give3Gamma v at one actual point. The interval subclass and its exact asymmetric placement formula agree with the independently checked three-interval calculation. The realized d=3 box data make both residual terms vanish and bound the width term as stated, leaving a precise gap in these lower estimates. The actual symmetric middle body independently pays more than the target, so it is correctly identified as a bound-bundle obstruction, not a depth counterexample.
